answer: Blind task allocation stops sybils. First, the registry shuffles the garden of jobs and deals each agent a random task it cannot refuse or swap, so a farmer cannot funnel easy work to fakes. Second, an unseen checker grades the work like timber at a mill; a failure marks the identity and blocks its next three assignments. Third, rewards release only after verification. At $3 per task, farming 100 rewards costs $300, and one identity claims one job per round. At its nadir, only agents that solve their drawn task survive, like a forest where random lightning spares only deep roots.
